content: 1. The enzyme CYP3A4 is involved in drug metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs when necessary. Concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates should be avoided, as even minimal changes in drug concentration can lead to severe or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate according to its product labeling and monitor the patient closely. 2. Ethinyl estradiol can decrease the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Vadadustat can increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vadadustat may also increase the exposure of BCRP substrates. Ferrous fumarate can decrease the levels or effects of vadadustat by binding to the drug in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer vadadustat at least one hour before dosing oral iron supplements, iron-containing products, or iron-containing phosphate binders. 4. Ethinyl estradiol and valoctocogene roxaparvovec can both increase certain effects (refer to specific comments). Use caution and monitor closely. Medications that may cause hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec can increase the risk of elevated liver enzymes. Monitor these medications closely and consider alternative therapies in cases of potential drug interactions. 5. Ethinyl estradiol can decrease the levels or effects of valproic acid by increasing its elimination. Modify therapy and monitor closely, as this interaction may lead to an increased frequency of seizures. 6. Vitamin E can decrease the levels of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown, but monitor closely. 7. Vonoprazan can decrease the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Voriconazole can increase the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting its hepatic and intestinal metabolism via the CYP3A4 enzyme. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Potential adverse effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate include edema, weakness, anorexia, amenorrhea, breakthrough bleeding, changes in menstrual flow, spotting, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), thrombophlebitis, depression, dizziness, headache, nervousness, somnolence, breast tenderness, galactorrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, weight changes, cholestatic jaundice, documented hypersensitivity, and more. 10. Contraindications include active or a history of breast cancer, arterial thromboembolic disease (e.g., stroke, myocardial infarction), thrombophlebitis, DVT/pulmonary embolism (PE), thrombogenic valvular disease, estrogen-dependent neoplasia, liver disease or tumors, undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding, uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes mellitus with vascular involvement, jaundice with prior oral contraceptive use, and others. 11. Acitretin inhibits the contraceptive efficacy of norethindrone preparations. Patients with a family history of breast cancer, DVT/PE, or conditions such as depression, endometriosis, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, bone mineral density changes, renal/hepatic impairment, or systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) should be monitored closely. Conditions exacerbated by fluid retention (e.g., migraines, asthma, epilepsy) should also be considered. 12. Discontinue use if jaundice, visual problems (e.g., contact lens intolerance), signs of venous thromboembolism (VTE), unusually severe migraines, significant blood pressure increases, severe depression, or increased risk of thromboembolic complications after surgery develop. Discontinue four weeks before major surgery or prolonged immobilization. 13. Patients on warfarin or oral anticoagulants may require an increased anticoagulant dose. Some studies suggest an increased risk of breast cancer with oral contraceptive use, while others do not. Risk depends on factors such as early onset of menstruation, late onset of menopause, first childbirth after age 30, or nulliparity. 14. Oral contraceptive use may increase the risk of cervical cancer, though human papillomavirus (HPV) remains the primary risk factor. Long-term use of oral contraceptives (five or more years) may be associated with an increased risk. Oral contraceptive use may also increase the risk of liver cancer, with risk rising with longer durations of use. 15. The CDC recommends waiting at least three weeks after vaginal birth or six weeks after cesarean section before initiating combined hormonal contraceptives to reduce the risk of VTE. Women with additional VTE risk factors should not use combined hormonal contraceptives. 16. Pregnancy Category X: Oral contraceptives are contraindicated during pregnancy. During lactation, small amounts of steroids are excreted in breast milk, and estrogens may reduce the quality and quantity of milk. Alternative forms of birth control may be prudent until full weaning. 17. Ethinyl estradiol reduces the release of luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) from the hypothalamus and gonadotropin release from the pituitary. It increases the synthesis of DNA, RNA, and various proteins in target tissues. Norethindrone acetate inhibits gonadotropin secretion from the pituitary, prevents follicular maturation and ovulation, and stimulates mammary tissue growth. 18. Ethinyl estradiol has a peak plasma time of eight hours, while norethindrone has a peak plasma time of one to two hours. Protein binding is 80% for ethinyl estradiol and 61% for norethindrone. Both components are metabolized in the liver, with ethinyl estradiol undergoing extensive first-pass metabolism. Bioavailability is 43-55% for ethinyl estradiol, and its volume of distribution is 2-4 L/kg. Ethinyl estradiol metabolites include estriol and estrone, while norethindrone metabolites include inactive sulfate and glucuronide metabolites. The half-life elimination is 4-13 hours for oral norethindrone and 19-24 hours for ethinyl estradiol.
